title: U.S. House · Georgia's 2nd Congressional District
area: Southwest Georgia, including Columbus and Albany.

context.text: Incumbent Sanford Bishop Jr. (D), who has represented the district since 1993, advanced unopposed from the Democratic primary. Matt Day won the Republican primary unopposed after A. Wayne Johnson and Chuck Hand did not make the ballot. Brandon Daley is also running, on the Communist Party line.

candidates.name: Sanford Bishop Jr.
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Georgia's 2nd Congressional District (since 1993)

summary.text: Sanford Bishop Jr. is the Democratic incumbent in Georgia's 2nd Congressional District, which he has represented since 1993. A lawyer and Army veteran, he served in both chambers of the Georgia legislature before his election to Congress in 1992. He is the Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies and is seeking re-election.

background.text: Born February 4, 1947, in Mobile, Alabama, the son of the first president of Bishop State Community College and a librarian.
Graduated from Morehouse College in 1968 and earned a law degree from Emory University School of Law in 1971.
Enlisted in the U.S. Army in 1969, completed basic training at Fort Moore, Georgia, and received an honorable discharge in 1971 after Advanced ROTC training.
Lived in Columbus, Georgia, from 1972 to 1996 and was the primary partner in the law firm Bishop and Buckner, P.C.
Served in the Georgia House of Representatives from 1977 to 1990 and in the Georgia Senate from 1991 to 1992, according to his official biography.
First elected to the U.S. House in 1992 and has served since 1993; his official biography says he is serving his seventeenth term.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee, as Ranking Member of its Agriculture, Rural Development, FDA and Related Agencies Subcommittee and a member of the Financial Services and General Government and Military Construction, Veterans Affairs subcommittees; before 2003 he served on the Agriculture, Veterans' Affairs, Post Office and Civil Service, and Intelligence committees.
Was a Senior Democratic Whip in the 112th and 113th Congresses; Georgia Trend magazine has named him among the 100 Most Influential Georgians several times.
According to his official biography, he is married to Vivian Creighton Bishop, has a daughter and a granddaughter, lives in Albany, Georgia, and is a deacon and trustee of Mount Zion Baptist Church.

priorities.text: Says he supports federal investments in infrastructure and transportation networks as fundamental to quality of life and the region's economy.

As a senior member of the Appropriations Committee, says he supports a responsible federal budget that funds programs that affect Americans' lives while drawing revenue from a tax code that is fair, balanced, and fiscally responsible.
Says ensuring veterans and their families are cared for after their service is a priority.

positions.summary: Says he strongly supports the Second Amendment, while also saying it is appropriately subject to reasonable, commonsense measures including background checks to limit access by those whose mental health or criminal history shows a lack of responsibility.
positions.quote: The Second Amendment to the United States Constitution, which Congressman Bishop strongly supports, is appropriately subject to reasonable, commonsense measures, including background checks to limit access by those whose mental health or criminal history demonstrates a lack of requisite responsibility.

positions.summary: Says immigration reform must strengthen border security by increasing law-enforcement manpower and providing the tools to enforce existing immigration laws and punish offenders.
positions.quote: Any immigration reform must include provisions that strengthen border security by increasing law enforcement manpower, utilizing new technology and fencing, and providing the tools, resources, and infrastructure necessary to enforce existing immigration laws and punish offenders.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, including the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration and Related Agencies; Financial Services and General Government; and Military Construction, Veterans Affairs and Related Agencies subcommittees, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Is a member of the Blue Dog Coalition, a group of fiscally conservative House Democrats.

candidates.name: Matt Day
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after A. Wayne Johnson and Chuck Hand did not make the ballot.

summary.text: Matt Day (legal name Benjamin Matthew Day) is the Republican nominee for Georgia's 2nd Congressional District. He is a business owner from Douglas, Georgia, with a background in the glazing and construction industries, and this is his first run for office. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports he calls himself a commonsense conservative.

background.text: Is from Douglas, Georgia, and is described by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution as a business owner.

According to Branch, he launched Glaziers on Demand in 2013, which supplied glass installation crews to sites in more than 40 states, and founded Glazier Nation in 2019, a staffing service for electricians, welders and crane operators on large construction projects.

Branch lists him as founder and owner of ChoreNab since 2025, a company applying an on-demand labor model to U.S. manufacturing plants; his campaign website lists glazing, construction and software development among his experience.
Has not held elected office; Branch describes this campaign as his first entry into politics. He was unopposed in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary, per Ballotpedia.
